findings.sourceReading: Will says it might have been better had Battler never returned; Clair says she might then have avoided the unforgivable crime of mass murder, although suffering would have continued. Both explicitly use kamoshirenai.
findings.alternative: Would clauses appropriately mark the unreal condition, but do not retain uncertainty about its result. In a way softens the sense in which the outcome is better, not the claim that it would have been better. The earlier year-earlier-or-later hypothesis remains tentative, so this is a local strengthening of two adjacent claims.

findings.sourceReading: Lion still does not understand, but resolves to hear the story without running away and to try to know. The following question asks what happened to bring about the crime.
findings.alternative: Kiku can mean ask, and the following question naturally supplies an asking act. Here nigezu ni follows Lion’s resistance to accepting the alternate life and Will’s injunction to listen; it commits Lion to confronting the testimony without fleeing. Straightforwardly does not retain that commitment or fear.

findings.sourceReading: The witch contrasts men’s fierce but short quarrels with women’s: no flames rise, but the source of fire or embers remain indefinitely.
findings.alternative: A steady flame conveys persistence and thus keeps one half of the comparison. It nevertheless contradicts the explicit absence of flames, replacing latent resentment with continuing visible combustion and weakening the contrast with men’s open flare-up.

findings.sourceReading: Shannon must make the resolve herself; it cannot be accomplished merely by Battler coming for her. His coming alone is insufficient.
findings.alternative: The surrounding insistence on Shannon’s own resolve can support its independence from his arrival, but it does not equate insufficiency with lack of necessity. The source negates merely arriving as an adequate cause; the English negates requiring the visit as a condition. The earlier promise remains a joint undertaking.

findings.sourceReading: Shannon realizes she had to become conscious of her resolve to step into this future: she must recognize her own decision and commitment.
findings.alternative: The ensuing acknowledgement that she has not reached that resolve yet makes the future demanding. How much determination will be needed is nevertheless an assessment of the degree of effort the future requires, rather than recognition of the resolve she herself must make; there is no quantity expression in the source.

findings.sourceReading: Shannon calls anxiety a betrayal of him, the person who promised to come for her in response to her resolve. Watashi no ketsui ni taishite modifies his promise, not a second object of betrayal.

findings.sourceReading: Will says words, once meaning resides in them, can influence a person’s life; careless words might even kill someone.
findings.alternative: Lion has just suggested misleading melodramatic phrasing, so differing interpretations are relevant context. Will’s broader formulation does not require multiple meanings: words that acquire meaning can direct a life even with one interpretation. The English narrows his general caution to semantic difference.
